collection_summary: This instance is a curated, source-defined, non-exhaustive set of transboundary rivers over 100 miles. Most rows come from Wikipedia's "Transboundary river" page section "List of major international transboundary rivers"; Oceania required supplementation from the Fly River and Sepik pages. It preserves an earlier minimal-supplement source set rather than the later broadened Wikipedia synthesis used for the >=1000 km sibling instance.
source_coverage_notes: Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, and South America rely on the cited "major international transboundary rivers" list rather than continent-specific exhaustive authorities. Oceania is not covered by that list excerpt and was supplemented with Fly and Sepik from their dedicated pages. The current 26 rows are therefore plausible for this minimal-supplement cited source set, but not validated as exhaustive for the broader natural-language query. Additional omitted rivers were later identified during work on the >=1000 km sibling instance; they were not retrofitted here so this artifact would remain a stable record of the earlier narrower curation choice.
decision_log: Adopted the minimal-change Path A interpretation from metadata review: preserve the instance as a source-defined curated set rather than an exhaustive global predicate result. Updated table_title, query_category, secondary_category, db_analog, and temporal_note accordingly. Kept operation_type=filter as the closest coarse label under the reframed task. Corrected the Europe/Rhone key to Europe/Rhône to match the cited source form. Deliberately kept this >100 miles instance as the earlier minimal-supplement variant rather than broadening it after later omission-finding work on the >=1000 km sibling.
normalization_decisions: River names follow cited source form where feasible. Applied source-form normalization for Rhône rather than preserving ASCII-only Rhone. Countries remain denormalized text lists because the schema declares Countries as text rather than a normalized one-to-many relation.
open_questions: If a future benchmark version wants the original exhaustive-filter interpretation, this instance should be rebuilt from continent-specific authoritative river sources rather than the current Wikipedia major-rivers list. If methodological consistency across sibling river instances becomes more important than preserving curation history, this >100 miles artifact should either be broadened with the same omission-finding strategy used for the >=1000 km instance or retired in favor of the broader sibling.
